2015-05-19 16:23 GMT+02:00 Zhang, Nancy <n...@wharton.upenn.edu>:
Dear Andre,

Thanks for your interest in CODEX.  I cc'd Yuchao, who is first author on the paper and who wrote the R package.

Answering your questions: 

1. This software can be used for both tumor (somatic CNA) and population based CNV analysis.  It has two running "modes", one for tumor and one for CNV.  Actually, the normalization model was first designed with CNVs in mind and then later expanded to include tumors.

2. Yes!  Yuchao recently modified and extended CODEX for targeted sequencing analysis.  But, you need a reasonable number of exons to fit a good "null" normalization model, that is, you can't just focus on regions with CNV, make sense?

Sounds like an interesting study, good luck!

Nancy


From: André Vidas Olsen [andre....@gmail.com]
Sent: Tuesday, May 19, 2015 7:13 AM
To: Zhang, Nancy
Subject: CODEX

Hi Nancy R. Zhang.

I'm starting to write my master's thesis which will include the analysis and detection of CNV's in WES data set between a control group and a case group consisting of patients with type 2 diabetes. The control-case groups are unmatched, and consists of targeted sequence regions of 244 genes. I have considered using the CODEX software and in this connection I have a few questions I would like to ask you:

1: Is this software primarily used for tumor studies, or is it applicable as a general CNV tool, which mean that I can use it for this diabetes association study?
2: Is it possible to use only these targeted sequenced gene regions instead of all exons within a chromosome and still get reasonable results?

I don't have the full data set yet, but it will consist of around 5000 samples with around 200X average coverage.


Best regards,
André

messages.subject: Re: CODEX processing entire chromosome?
parts:
Hi Andre,

Yes, please refer to below for codes that process the entire genome all at once (this is for targeted sequencing but they work in the same way). Note that when you do segmentation though, you need to be careful by separating the chromosomes or just use a hard thresholding procedure on the ratio of Y/lambda.

CODEX for targeted sequencing:
We've adapted CODEX for targeted sequencing. Refer to codes attached (need to source segment_targeted.R for gene based segmentation):
codex_targeted.R
segment_targeted.R

Yuchao

Dear Andre,

Thanks for your interest in CODEX.  I cc'd Yuchao, who is first author on the paper and who wrote the R package.

Answering your questions: 

1. This software can be used for both tumor (somatic CNA) and population based CNV analysis.  It has two running "modes", one for tumor and one for CNV.  Actually, the normalization model was first designed with CNVs in mind and then later expanded to include tumors.

2. Yes!  Yuchao recently modified and extended CODEX for targeted sequencing analysis.  But, you need a reasonable number of exons to fit a good "null" normalization model, that is, you can't just focus on regions with CNV, make sense?

Sounds like an interesting study, good luck!

Nancy
